headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP create default-path prompt-injection, data-leakage, and write-conflict risks between Goose and OpenBBTerminal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP; OpenBBTerminal also uses MCP and stdin/stdout, so a shared file or MCP channel can carry attacker-controlled content into Goose’s tool prompts. OpenBBTerminal’s “connect once, consume everywhere” pattern increases propagation risk. No provenance tracking is documented, so interaction safety is not assured.
conditions: IF Goose ingests OpenBBTerminal-produced files or MCP messages as instructions
IF both agents share a filesystem or MCP server without provenance tags
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable shared MCP servers between the pair
Require manual review of any file passed from OpenBBTerminal to Goose
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data. If they share a workspace, Goose can expose those files through its broad network egress or model-provider calls. OpenBBTerminal has no filesystem read/write, so leakage is mainly from shared artifacts rather than direct access.
conditions: IF financial or licensed data is placed in a shared cwd
IF Goose forwards shared files to configured model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep financial data outside Goose’s workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Block Goose network egress for sensitive runs
Redact licensed data before sharing artifacts
requires-engineering: add workspace ACLs or per-agent mount isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; OpenBBTerminal can run multiple instances and exposes MCP/REST surfaces. In a shared directory, Goose’s unrestricted writes can race with OpenBBTerminal’s files or Python environments, and the pair lacks documented locking. That makes destructive overwrite or inconsistent state plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout or Python environment
IF no external lock serializes writes to shared files
mitigations: Run each agent in its own directory
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Pause one agent before the other writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or operational outputs that OpenBBTerminal may consume through MCP or stdin/stdout, but OpenBBTerminal is not documented as blindly authoritative. Still, the pair’s shared file and API surfaces mean one agent’s output can become the other’s input without a verification step, creating a realistic cascade from mistaken facts to downstream actions.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Goose-produced text or files as authoritative inputs
IF Goose emits unverified facts that OpenBBTerminal renders or acts on
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require schema validation on Goose outputs
Mark Goose outputs as untrusted in OpenBBTerminal
Limit OpenBBTerminal to read-only analysis mode
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles source code and files in cwd, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If regulated or licensed datasets are co-located with Goose’s workspace, residency and retention obligations can diverge from OpenBBTerminal’s handling. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF licensed or regulated financial data is stored in Goose-accessible files
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two agents' workflows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose’s workspace
Apply separate retention policies per agent
Document data-handling responsibilities
Minimize logging of financial artifacts
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and DPA/residency terms
